🐾 Found it!

Matt worked on **JP Morgan Chase’s** ACCESS Next Generation payments platform from **August 2009** to **June 2012**, serving as Technology Delivery Lead and Senior Technology Architecture Manager. The bank was consolidating regional treasury systems into a unified global portal, but Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform did not provide all the payment modules, security controls, and workflows its clients required. Payment connectivity across **12 countries** involved different formats, protocols, and regulatory requirements, while legacy entitlement changes took days of manual configuration.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He defined the onshore-offshore engagement model and spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, coordinating with bank stakeholders in Chicago and NY/NJ. He worked with enterprise architects, security specialists, regional compliance officers, and developers to determine where WebSeries configuration ended and custom engineering was required.

His delivery scope included ACH credits and direct debits, Fedwire and international wires, FX/cross-border payments, and federal tax payments. He also designed the centralized gateway for message transformation, protocol translation, and routing. Around those payment flows, he built Message Authentication Code verification, payment-type-specific permissions, sanctions screening, and integrations with transaction monitoring. The redesigned administration engine reduced entitlement management from days to minutes through role-based profiles and bulk permission changes.

Matt also led payments data migration, preserving client configurations, entitlement structures, transaction histories, and compliance traceability without disrupting live payment operations. He coordinated regional launches around regulatory readiness rather than a single global deployment, and owned production incident response and leadership updates.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, serving **135,000+** corporations, financial institutions, governments, and municipalities across **180+ countries**. Its payments gateway gave corporate treasurers a single entry point across **12 countries**, replacing fragmented regional integrations.

🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009 to June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s global corporate banking portal. Treasury operations ran across separate regional and legacy systems, with different payment formats, client configurations, and entitlement structures. Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform provided the foundation, but the bank needed payment capabilities and controls beyond its out-of-box offering, under aggressive delivery timelines.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank practitioners across the US, Mumbai, and Bangalore. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working through where native platform functionality ended and bespoke engineering was required.

He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and federal tax payment modules. The work included NACHA file validation, foreign exchange engine integration, and Message Authentication Code security so corporate users could verify payment integrity before release. He also built payment-type-specific permissions, such as allowing wire approval without permitting FX initiation, alongside sanctions screening and risk-based approval controls.

For connectivity, Matt designed the centralized payments gateway handling message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**. Corporate treasurers gained a single entry point for wire, ACH, and cross-border transfers instead of separate local logins and regional payment systems.

He also led the payments data migration, preserving client configurations, entitlement structures, transaction histories, and compliance traceability with **zero disruption to live payment operations**. His advanced user administration engine replaced individual permission changes with bulk grouping and role-based profiles, reducing entitlement management from **days to minutes**.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, consolidating regional systems into a unified portal serving **135,000+ clients** across **180+ countries**. Matt also owned on-call and critical production incident response for the payment engine, coordinating root-cause analysis across bank, offshore, and vendor teams.
